data.name: Adineh
data.gender_notes: Adineh is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'adna' meaning 'noble' or 'delicate'. In Islamic culture, it is believed that this name signifies a person of high moral character and deep spiritual understanding. The name Adineh carries the meaning “Noble, Delicate” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Adineh usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, delicate and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Adineh belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Noble, Delicate.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adineh total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

He was a student of the great Persian philosopher and scholar Al-Ghazali and is considered one of the leading figures of the Islamic Golden Age. Adineh is best known for his works on logic, ethics, and philosophy, and his influence on Islamic thought can still be felt today.

historical_references.reference: Adineh was also known as Adh-Dhahabi, and he was a prominent scholar and historian during the 13th century. He is most famous for his biographical work 'Tarikh al-Islam', which is a comprehensive history of Islamic scholarship, and for his work 'Siyar A'lam an-Nubala', which is a biographical dictionary of Islamic scholars. Adineh's works have been invaluable resources for scholars studying the history of Islamic thought and scholarship.
